newsitem.title: BELARUS: Thousands join anti-president protest in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Thousands join anti-president protest in Belarus.

text.p: At least 3,000 people demonstrated against President Alexander Lukashenko in Belarus on Friday, waving flags, blowing whistles and shouting "Down with Luka."

The mostly young crowd handed in petitions to the embassies of France, Britain, Italy and Germany and made their way towards the U.S. embassy. Special OMON forces blocked off the president's building.
The protesters waved banners reading "Belarus into Europe" and shouted slogans against Lukashenko and his pro-Russian policies.
Nationalists in the republic of 10 million people bordering Russia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine want Belarus to look west towards Europe rather than east towards Russia.

They find solace in criticism from European institutions of Lukashenko's authoritarian approach, especially since he won a controversial referendum in November to seize broad powers and rewrite the constitution.

The Council of Europe said the new constitution failed to meet minimum human rights standards while Europe's top security body, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, has repeatedly called on Belarus to restore democracy.
